document_title: Permian Resources names two AI tools and prints no measured result for either
_note: Slide strings read off the render report's text nodes and each frame's own source line by build_copy.py.
caption:
AI for runtime. The record runtimes went to power and compression.

Permian Resources named two AI tools in its November 4th release. An artificial lift monitor is there to increase runtime. A second feeds its subsurface data to large language models.

Third quarter output was 457,528 barrels of oil equivalent a day. The release prints no measured result for either AI tool.

Its 2025 annual report put about 67% of its net leasehold in Texas. Neither filing says which wells the monitor watches. On May 21st the Texas Tribune reported the Railroad Commission said it was not aware of any use of AI by oil and gas companies. The same article quoted experts and analysts saying AI is reshaping how Permian operators handle produced water.

The Commission meets next on November 17th. How much of those record runtimes is the monitor's?

#DelawareBasin #PermianBasin #RailroadCommission

S1.headline: The artificial lift has a new watcher
S1.body: Permian Resources told investors on November 4th that its production team has deployed an AI-powered artificial lift monitoring system. The pump jack is drawn to illustrate.

Permian Resources told investors on November 4th that its production team has deployed an AI-powered artificial lift monitoring system. The pump jack is drawn to illustrate.

S2.headline: Two AI tools, one earnings release
S2.body: One monitors its artificial lift. The other feeds its subsurface data into large language models to evaluate wellbore placement and optimize drilling parameters.
strings: Two AI tools, one earnings release
One monitors its artificial lift. The other feeds its subsurface data into large language models to evaluate wellbore placement and optimize drilling parameters.

S3.headline: Its stated goal is more runtime
S3.body: The release says the monitor is there to increase runtime and optimize well performance. It credits record runtimes to power and compression projects.
strings: Its stated goal is more runtime
The release says the monitor is there to increase runtime and optimize well performance. It credits record runtimes to power and compression projects.

S4.headline: Language models, aimed at the wellbore
S4.body: The release says the company is combining its subsurface data with large language models. The bands are drawn to illustrate and are not to scale.
strings: Language models, aimed at the wellbore
The release says the company is combining its subsurface data with large language models. The bands are drawn to illustrate and are not to scale.

S5.headline: Output rose 22 percent in a quarter
S5.body: Total production averaged 457,528 barrels of oil equivalent a day. The release ties none of that rise to either AI tool.

Total production averaged 457,528 barrels of oil equivalent a day. The release ties none of that rise to either AI tool.

S6.headline: Crude is a little under half of its output
S6.body: Crude oil averaged 208,029 barrels a day in the third quarter. The gauge's target sits at that share of everything the company produced.
strings: Crude is a little under half of its output

S7.headline: About 67 percent of its leasehold was in Texas
S7.body: Its 2025 annual report put about 67% of its net leasehold in Texas and 33% in New Mexico. Neither the release nor the annual report says which wells the monitor watches.

S8.headline: The regulator was not aware of any AI use
S8.body: On May 21st the Texas Tribune reported the Railroad Commission said it was not aware of any use of AI by oil and gas companies. The release came 167 days later.

S9.headline: Who checks what the watcher finds?
